A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MVAR research, with matching authors, core methodology, and original experiments. The complete text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original ImageNet generation results, memory and timing measurements, component ablations, attention analyses, and generated examples.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds experiments on higher-resolution ImageNet, CelebA, FFHQ, larger models, and training sensitivity.

M1.justification: The adjacent-scale factorization, spatial neighborhood attention, cross-entropy objective, and cache-free inference remain unchanged. Expanded explanations of mixed training and CUDA kernels document implementation; the additional training schedules are experimental variants rather than a replacement of the proposed method.

E1.justification: v1 evaluates ImageNet at 256x256. v2 retains this coverage and adds ImageNet at 512x512, CelebA at 256x256 and 512x512, and FFHQ at 256x256 (Appendix D), substantially extending domain and resolution coverage.

E2.justification: The comparator membership in Tables 1–4 is retained. Added dataset and scalability experiments continue comparing MVAR with VAR; additional model depths and concatenated-versus-mixed training are configuration controls rather than new baseline methods.

E3.justification: Appendix D introduces 100-epoch ImageNet-512 training with a different scale sequence and grouping, 2B-model experiments, new dataset splits and batch sizes, and a d12 training-ratio study using 50 epochs and batch size 64. These are added protocols. The exact ImageNet-512 configuration remains somewhat ambiguous: D.1 references d20 settings while Table 6 labels the models d16.

E4.justification: Beyond retaining v1's component, conditioning-prefix, and neighborhood ablations, v2 tests neighborhood sensitivity across face datasets and resolutions (Table 9). Figure 9 adds concatenated-versus-mixed training comparisons and training-ratio sensitivity curves, directly examining the robustness of the memory-saving training strategy.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The added curves compare training configurations over epochs, not uncertainty across repeated runs.

E6.justification: Tables 6–9, Figure 9, and additional qualitative comparisons substantially expand the results. Newly reported MVAR/VAR FIDs include 7.55/8.03 on ImageNet-512 and 1.33/2.65 for 2B models on CelebA; these are new settings, not improvements over matched v1 runs. Existing generation scores are retained, while Table 2 changes VAR-d16's KV-cache value from 5,440 to 5,704 MB.

T1.justification: Equations 1–12, the Markov assumptions, and the computational-complexity derivations are retained. The complexity appendix moves from Appendix B to Appendix A without substantive mathematical changes.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about Markovian conditioning, O(Nk) attention, cache elimination, generation quality, and memory savings. Added appendix experiments provide broader support without redefining the headline contributions.

C2.justification: Appendix D interprets the new results as evidence of generalization, scalability, and limited sensitivity to neighborhood size and larger training ratios. It also qualifies the new comparisons as constrained by available compute. The original mechanism explanations and limitations paragraph remain substantively unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 substantially expands workflow documentation: CUDA handling, mixed-training iteration cycles, attention-visualization sampling and averaging, and splits, budgets, and scale sequences for new experiments. It corrects the first-eight-scale token count from 256 to 255. Access instructions change from a direct code/model repository pointer to a project page and promised release; actual resource availability is not established by the PDFs.

R1.justification: v2 adds Liu et al. (2015) for CelebA and Karras et al. (2019) for FFHQ, and removes Salimans et al. (2016), Improved Techniques for Training GANs. Positioning relative to VAR and other generative approaches remains unchanged; most bibliography changes are formatting.

P1.justification: Most existing prose is retained. v2 converts contributions to bullets, introduces related-work subsections, incorporates the causal-mask discussion into the methodology, reorganizes appendices, and adds an appendix contents list and disclosure statements. These are limited narrative changes alongside the added scientific material.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables 6–9, training-ratio plots, a higher-resolution comparison, and several comparative image galleries. It also changes the document template and table layouts and moves the causal-mask diagram into the main text. The original appendix figures are retained as Figures 10 and 15, rather than replaced.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens validation beyond v1's ImageNet-256 experiments. Appendix D tests higher resolution, additional data distributions, a 2B model, and sensitivity of the training strategy and neighborhood choice, addressing important gaps in evidence for scalability and robustness. Additional implementation documentation improves reproducibility. Some new configuration reporting remains ambiguous, particularly in D.1, but the broader controlled evidence provides a substantial net quality gain.
